topics.name: Joshua: overview
topics.description: Joshua records Israel crossing the Jordan after Moses' death (1:1-2), taking and dividing the land, and Joshua's closing call to serve the LORD at Shechem, ending with his death (24:29).
evidence: Say how the book begins with the death of Moses and ends with the death of Joshua
Name the three parts: entering and conquering, dividing the land, and the farewell charges
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline the book of Joshua from the crossing of the Jordan to the covenant at Shechem?

topics.name: The LORD commissions Joshua
topics.description: After Moses dies, the LORD tells Joshua to lead the people over the Jordan, promises to be with him, and charges him to keep the law; Joshua then orders the people to prepare and the eastern tribes pledge their help.
evidence: Retell what the LORD told Joshua after Moses died
Say what Joshua was told to do with the book of the law (1:7-8)
Explain what Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh promised (1:12-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what God said to Joshua at the start of the book?

topics.name: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
topics.description: Joshua sends two men to Jericho, where Rahab hides them, confesses that the LORD is God in heaven and earth, and secures their oath to spare her family, marked by a scarlet cord.
evidence: Retell how Rahab hid the spies
Say what Rahab had heard about the LORD (2:9-11)
Describe the promise the men made and the sign of the scarlet line (2:12-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Rahab did for the spies and what they promised her?

topics.name: Crossing the Jordan
topics.description: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, its waters are cut off, and Israel crosses on dry ground; twelve stones are taken from the river as a memorial for children to ask about.
evidence: Retell how Israel crossed the Jordan
Explain what the twelve stones were for (4:6-7, 4:21-24)
Say what Joshua 4:23 compares the crossing to
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israel crossed the Jordan and why the stones were set up?

topics.name: Circumcision, Passover and the captain of the LORD's host
topics.description: At Gilgal the new generation is circumcised, Israel keeps the passover and eats the produce of the land as the manna ceases, and Joshua meets the captain of the LORD's host near Jericho.
evidence: Explain why Joshua circumcised the people (5:4-7)
Say what happened to the manna (5:12)
Describe Joshua's meeting by Jericho and what he was told to do (5:13-15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Gilgal before Jericho?

topics.name: The fall of Jericho
topics.description: Israel marches round Jericho for seven days with the ark and trumpets, the wall falls at the shout, the city is devoted to destruction, and Rahab and her household are saved.
evidence: Retell the instructions for marching round Jericho (6:3-5)
Say what happened on the seventh day (6:15-20)
Explain why Rahab and her household were spared (6:22-25)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jericho fell and who was saved?

topics.name: Achan's sin and defeat at Ai
topics.description: Israel is routed at Ai because Achan took devoted things from Jericho; Joshua prays, the LORD reveals the sin by lot, and Achan confesses and is stoned.
evidence: Retell why Israel lost at Ai (7:1, 7:10-12)
Describe how Achan was found out and what he confessed (7:16-21)
Say what the LORD calls the people's act in 7:11
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Israel was defeated at Ai?

topics.name: The taking of Ai
topics.description: The LORD tells Joshua not to fear and to ambush Ai; the city is drawn out, burned, and taken, and Israel may take its spoil.
evidence: Retell the ambush plan and how it worked
Say how this differs from Jericho regarding spoil (8:2)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israel took Ai the second time?

topics.name: The law read at Mount Ebal
topics.description: Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal as Moses commanded, writes a copy of the law on stones, and reads all its blessings and cursings to the whole assembly.
evidence: Say what Joshua built and wrote on Mount Ebal
Explain who heard the law read (8:33-35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Israel did at Mount Ebal after Ai?

topics.name: The Gibeonite deception
topics.description: The people of Gibeon pretend to come from a far country and trick Israel into a treaty without asking the LORD; when found out, they are made woodcutters and water carriers and spared because of the oath.
evidence: Retell how Gibeon deceived Israel
Say what Israel failed to do (9:14)
Explain why Israel did not destroy them (9:18-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the Gibeonites tricked Joshua and what happened next?

topics.name: The LORD fights at Gibeon
topics.description: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon; Joshua marches all night, the LORD sends hailstones, the sun stands still at Joshua's word, and the five kings are caught in a cave at Makkedah and put to death.
evidence: Say why Israel went to help Gibeon
Describe what the LORD did in the battle (10:10-14)
Say what happened to the five kings (10:16-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the five kings attacked Gibeon?

topics.name: The southern campaign
topics.description: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir and the surrounding country, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
evidence: List some of the southern cities Joshua took
Say who fought for Israel (10:42)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some cities Joshua took in the south and say who gave the victory?

topics.name: The northern campaign and the whole land taken
topics.description: Jabin of Hazor gathers northern kings at the waters of Merom; the LORD delivers them to Israel, Hazor is burned, and the summary says Joshua took the land according to what the LORD told Moses and the land rested from war.
evidence: Say who gathered at Merom and what the LORD told Joshua
Explain what chapter 11 says about Gibeon being the only city to make peace (11:19)
Say how the chapter says Joshua obeyed Moses' commands (11:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell about the battle at Merom and the summary of Joshua's conquest?

topics.name: The list of defeated kings
topics.description: Joshua 12 lists the two kings Moses defeated east of the Jordan and thirty-one kings Joshua defeated to the west.
evidence: Name Sihon and Og as the kings on the east side (12:1-6)
Say how many kings are listed west of the Jordan (12:24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the list in Joshua 12 shows?

topics.name: Land still to be possessed and the eastern tribes
topics.description: The LORD tells the aged Joshua that much land remains and orders it divided; the chapter recalls Moses' gifts east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and that the Levites' inheritance was the LORD himself.
evidence: Say what the LORD told old Joshua (13:1, 13:6-7)
Name the tribes that received land from Moses east of the Jordan
Say what the Levites' inheritance was (13:14, 13:33)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Joshua 13 says remained and who already had land?

topics.name: Caleb receives Hebron
topics.description: Caleb recalls Moses' oath at Kadesh and, at eighty-five, asks for the hill country of Hebron; Joshua blesses him, Caleb drives out the sons of Anak, and Othniel wins Debir and Achsah.
evidence: Say why Caleb says he deserves Hebron (14:8-9)
Retell how Othniel won Achsah (15:16-17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Caleb received Hebron?

topics.name: Judah's inheritance
topics.description: The lot for Judah is described by its borders and cities, and the text notes that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
evidence: Say what chapter 15 says about the Jebusites in Jerusalem (15:63)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Joshua 15 describes and what Judah failed to do?

topics.name: Ephraim and Manasseh's inheritance
topics.description: The lots for Ephraim and Manasseh are described, the daughters of Zelophehad receive their inheritance, Canaanites in Gezer remain, and the house of Joseph complains of too little land and is told to clear the hill country.
evidence: Name the two tribes of the house of Joseph
Say what Zelophehad's daughters asked for (17:3-4)
Say what Joshua told the house of Joseph to do (17:14-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Ephraim and Manasseh received and what they were told to do?

topics.name: Shiloh and the seven remaining tribes
topics.description: Israel sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh; Joshua rebukes the seven tribes for delaying, sends men to describe the land in seven parts, and casts lots for Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan before receiving his own city.
evidence: Say what Joshua told the seven tribes (18:3)
List the remaining tribes who received lots
Say what city Joshua received (19:49-50)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the last seven tribes got their land?

topics.name: Cities of refuge
topics.description: The LORD tells Joshua to appoint cities of refuge where someone who killed unwittingly can flee from the avenger of blood; six cities are named, three on each side of the Jordan.
evidence: Say who could flee to a city of refuge and who could not be handed over to the avenger (20:3-5)
Name some of the six cities (20:7-8)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what a city of refuge was for?

topics.name: Cities for the Levites and the promises kept
topics.description: The Levites receive forty-eight cities from the tribes by lot, and the chapter ends by saying the LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to their fathers, gave them rest, and not one good word failed.
evidence: Say why the Levites got cities rather than a tribal territory (21:2)
Say what 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Joshua 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises?

topics.name: The altar of witness
topics.description: Joshua sends the eastern tribes home; they build a great altar by the Jordan, the western tribes prepare for war, and Phinehas and ten princes confront them, learning that the altar is a witness and not for sacrifice.
evidence: Say why the western tribes were alarmed (22:11-20)
Explain what the eastern tribes said the altar was for (22:24-29)
Say how the dispute ended and what the altar was named (22:30-34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of the altar by the Jordan and how Israel avoided war?

topics.name: Joshua's farewell charge
topics.description: Old Joshua calls Israel to keep the law, cling to the LORD and avoid the remaining nations, warning that if they turn away and break the covenant, the LORD will bring evil on them.
evidence: Say what Joshua told Israel to cling to
Say what Joshua warned would happen if they served other gods (23:12-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain Joshua's warning in chapter 23?

topics.name: Choose this day: the covenant at Shechem
topics.description: At Shechem Joshua recounts God's acts from Abraham to the conquest, urges Israel to choose whom to serve, makes a covenant with the people, and sets up a stone of witness before dying at 110.
evidence: Say what Joshua and his house decided (24:15)
Retell the history Joshua recounted (24:2-13)
Say what Joshua did that day and where he was buried (24:25-30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Shechem and what Joshua said about choosing whom to serve?

topics.name: Judges: overview
topics.description: Judges tells of Israel after Joshua's death, repeatedly falling into idolatry, being oppressed, crying out and being delivered by judges, and ends with the refrain that there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
evidence: Describe the repeating pattern in Judges 2:11-19
Name several judges and the enemies they faced
Say what 21:25 says about Israel at the end
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and deliverance in Judges?

topics.name: Judah's victories and tribes that failed to drive out the Canaanites
topics.description: After Joshua's death Judah and Simeon fight first, Othniel wins Achsah, and the chapter lists tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants; the angel of the LORD at Bochim says this disobedience will leave the nations as snares.
evidence: Say who went up first against the Canaanites (1:1-2)
Name some tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants (1:27-33)
Say what the angel of the LORD said and how the people responded (2:1-5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Joshua died and why the angel spoke at Bochim?

topics.name: The cycle of the judges
topics.description: After Joshua's generation a new generation forgets the LORD and serves Baal; he gives them to enemies, raises up judges to deliver them, and leaves nations to test Israel, who also intermarry and serve their gods.
evidence: Retell the pattern in 2:11-19
Say why the LORD left nations in the land (2:20-22, 3:1-4)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the pattern that repeats through the book of Judges?

topics.name: Othniel delivers Israel
topics.description: Israel serves the king of Mesopotamia for eight years; when they cry out the LORD raises up Othniel, on whom the Spirit comes, and the land has rest forty years.
evidence: Retell the first oppression and deliverance in Judges
Say what is said about the Spirit of the LORD and Othniel (3:10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Othniel became Israel's first judge?

topics.name: Ehud and Shamgar
topics.description: Israel serves Eglon of Moab eighteen years; the left-handed Ehud kills Eglon with a hidden dagger, leads Israel to defeat Moab, and the land has rest eighty years; Shamgar also delivers Israel.
evidence: Retell how Ehud killed Eglon
Say what Ehud did after escaping (3:27-30)
Say what Shamgar did (3:31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Ehud and how Moab was subdued?

topics.name: Deborah, Barak and Jael
topics.description: Under Jabin's oppression Deborah the prophetess calls Barak to fight Sisera; the LORD routs Sisera's chariots and Jael kills Sisera in her tent.
evidence: Retell why Deborah summoned Barak (4:6-7)
Say how the LORD gave victory (4:14-16)
Say what Jael did (4:17-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how God gave victory over Sisera through Deborah, Barak and Jael?

topics.name: The song of Deborah and Barak
topics.description: Deborah and Barak sing praise to the LORD for the victory, honour the tribes that came and rebuke those that stayed away, bless Jael, and picture Sisera's mother waiting in vain.
evidence: Say who sings the song and whom it praises (5:1-3)
Name tribes praised or blamed (5:14-18, 5:23)
Say how long the land had rest (5:31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the song of Deborah celebrates?

topics.name: The LORD calls Gideon
topics.description: Midian oppresses Israel seven years and Israel cries out; the angel of the LORD calls Gideon, who tears down his father's altar of Baal by night, and then asks for a fleece sign.
evidence: Retell how the angel of the LORD found Gideon
Say what Gideon did to the altar of Baal (6:25-32)
Describe the fleece sign (6:36-40)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how God called Gideon and what signs he asked for?

topics.name: Gideon's three hundred
topics.description: The LORD reduces Gideon's army to three hundred; after hearing a Midianite dream, Gideon surrounds the camp with trumpets, pitchers and lamps and the LORD sets the Midianites against each other.
evidence: Say why the LORD reduced the army (7:2)
Describe how the three hundred attacked (7:16-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Gideon defeated Midian with three hundred men?

topics.name: Gideon pursues Midian and refuses to rule
topics.description: Gideon calms Ephraim, punishes Succoth and Penuel for refusing him bread, kills the kings Zebah and Zalmunna, declines Israel's offer to rule, but makes an ephod that becomes a snare; after his death Israel turns again to Baal.
evidence: Say how Gideon answered the offer to rule (8:22-23)
Say what became a snare (8:27)
Say what Israel did after Gideon died (8:33-35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Gideon did after the victory and what happened when he died?

topics.name: Abimelech kills his brothers; Jotham's fable
topics.description: Abimelech persuades Shechem to make him king and kills Gideon's seventy sons except Jotham, who tells a fable of the trees and the bramble and pronounces a curse.
evidence: Say how Abimelech became king (9:1-6)
Retell Jotham's fable and the curse (9:7-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Abimelech did and what Jotham said from Mount Gerizim?

topics.name: The fall of Abimelech
topics.description: God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; Abimelech destroys Shechem and its tower, and at Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head; the text says God repaid his wickedness and Jotham's curse came.
evidence: Say what happened between Abimelech and Shechem
Describe how Abimelech died (9:50-54)
Say how the text explains these events (9:56-57)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jotham's curse came true for Abimelech and Shechem?

topics.name: Tola, Jair, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon
topics.description: Short notices list judges who ruled after Abimelech and Jephthah, with their tribes, years and burial places.
evidence: Name two or more of these judges and say how long they judged
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some of the judges mentioned briefly in Judges?

topics.name: Israel cries to the LORD under the Philistines and Ammon
topics.description: Israel again serves other gods and is oppressed by the Philistines and Ammon; the LORD tells them to cry to their chosen gods, but when they confess and put away the foreign gods, his soul is grieved for their misery.
evidence: Say what the LORD answered first (10:11-14)
Say what Israel did next (10:15-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Israel responded when the LORD refused at first to deliver them?

topics.name: Jephthah is made head of Gilead
topics.description: Jephthah, driven out by his half-brothers, is asked back by the elders of Gilead to fight Ammon; he first sends messengers recounting how Israel came to the land.
evidence: Say why Jephthah was expelled and why he was recalled (11:1-8)
Summarise his message to the king of Ammon (11:12-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jephthah became leader of Gilead?

topics.name: Jephthah's vow
topics.description: The Spirit of the LORD comes on Jephthah, who vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if the LORD gives victory; the LORD delivers Ammon, and his only daughter comes out to meet him.
evidence: Say what Jephthah vowed (11:30-31)
Say who met him and how she answered (11:34-36)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jephthah vowed and what followed?

topics.name: Jephthah and Ephraim
topics.description: The men of Ephraim complain that Jephthah did not call them; Gilead fights them and uses the word Shibboleth at the Jordan fords; Jephthah judges six years.
evidence: Say why Ephraim was angry (12:1)
Say how the Gileadites identified Ephraimites (12:5-6)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the word Shibboleth was used for?

topics.name: The birth of Samson
topics.description: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's barren wife that she will bear a son who will be a Nazarite and begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines; Manoah offers a burnt offering and Samson is born.
evidence: Say what the son was to avoid (13:4-5, 13:7)
Say what Manoah and his wife saw at the offering (13:19-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD promised Manoah's wife?

topics.name: Samson's wedding riddle
topics.description: Samson wants a Philistine wife, kills a lion by the Spirit, and poses a riddle at his feast; his wife tells the answer, and he kills thirty men at Ashkelon and leaves; she is given to his companion.
evidence: Retell the riddle and how it was answered
Note that 14:4 says this was of the LORD, seeking occasion against the Philistines
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Samson's riddle?

topics.name: Samson burns the fields and fights at Lehi
topics.description: Samson burns the Philistines' grain with foxes carrying firebrands after his wife is given away; Judah binds him and hands him over, but the Spirit comes on him and he kills a thousand with a jawbone; God provides water.
evidence: Say why Samson burned the Philistine fields
Say what Judah did and what Samson did at Lehi (15:9-17)
Say how Samson's thirst was met (15:18-19)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened between Samson, the Philistines and Judah?

topics.name: Samson and Delilah
topics.description: Samson carries off the gates of Gaza, then loves Delilah, who is bribed by the Philistine lords; after three false answers he reveals his Nazarite hair, it is cut, the LORD departs from him, and he is blinded and imprisoned.
evidence: Say what Delilah asked and how Samson answered
Say what Samson told Delilah about his hair (16:17)
Say what happened when his hair was cut (16:19-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Samson lost his strength?

topics.name: The death of Samson
topics.description: At the Philistines' feast to Dagon, the blind Samson prays to the LORD and pulls down the pillars, killing more in his death than in his life.
evidence: Say why the Philistines gathered (16:23-25)
Say what Samson prayed and did (16:28-30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Samson died?

topics.name: Micah's idols and his Levite priest
topics.description: Micah of Ephraim returns stolen silver to his mother, makes images and an ephod, and hires a Levite from Bethlehem as his priest; the text notes there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
evidence: Say what Micah made and whom he hired as priest
Say what 17:6 says about Israel then
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong in Micah's house?

topics.name: The Danites take Micah's priest and settle Laish
topics.description: The tribe of Dan sends spies who meet Micah's Levite; six hundred armed Danites take Micah's images and priest, capture the peaceful city of Laish and rename it Dan.
evidence: Say what the Danites took from Micah
Say what they did to Laish (18:27-29)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the Danites came to live in the city of Dan?

topics.name: The Levite and his concubine at Gibeah
topics.description: A Levite and his concubine lodge at Gibeah of Benjamin; men of the city assault the house, she is abused through the night and found dead at the door, and he sends her divided body through Israel; the text says no such deed had been seen since Egypt.
evidence: Say where the events took place
Say how Israel reacted to the sign sent to all the tribes (19:29-30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Gibeah and what the Levite did?

topics.name: Israel's war against Benjamin
topics.description: Israel assembles at Mizpeh and demands the guilty men of Gibeah; Benjamin refuses and defeats Israel twice, but after Israel inquires of the LORD and uses an ambush, Benjamin is nearly destroyed.
evidence: Say why Israel went to war with Benjamin
Say what happened in the first two battles and the third (20:21-25, 20:35)
Say how many Benjamite men escaped (20:47)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the war between Israel and Benjamin went?

topics.name: Wives for Benjamin
topics.description: Israel grieves that a tribe is missing; having sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, they take wives from Jabesh-gilead and from the daughters of Shiloh; the book ends noting there was no king in Israel.
evidence: Say what oath Israel had sworn (21:1)
Say how the remaining Benjamites got wives (21:10-23)
Say how the book ends (21:25)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Israel dealt with the tribe of Benjamin after the war?

topics.name: Ruth: overview
topics.description: Ruth, set in the days when the judges ruled, follows Naomi and her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth from loss in Moab to marriage with Boaz in Bethlehem and the birth of Obed, the grandfather of David.
evidence: Say where the story is set and when
Say how the book ends with David's line (4:17-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarise the book of Ruth from Moab to the birth of Obed?

topics.name: Naomi and Ruth return from Moab
topics.description: A famine drives Elimelech's family to Moab, where he and his sons die; Naomi returns to Bethlehem, and Ruth refuses to leave her, pledging that Naomi's people and God will be hers.
evidence: Retell why Naomi's family went to Moab and what happened to them
Say what Ruth promised Naomi (1:16-17)
Say what Naomi asked to be called and why (1:20-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Ruth said to Naomi and why Naomi returned to Bethlehem?

topics.name: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field
topics.description: Ruth gleans barley and lands in the field of Boaz, a kinsman of Elimelech, who shows her kindness and protection and tells her to stay with his young women; Naomi calls him one of their near kinsmen.
evidence: Say how Boaz treated Ruth (2:8-16)
Say what Boaz said about the LORD's reward for Ruth (2:12)
Say what Naomi said about Boaz (2:20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Boaz showed kindness to Ruth?

topics.name: Ruth at the threshing floor
topics.description: At Naomi's direction Ruth goes to Boaz at the threshing floor and asks him as a near kinsman to spread his skirt over her; he praises her character, says there is a nearer kinsman, and promises to act.
evidence: Say what Naomi told Ruth to do
Say what Boaz said about the nearer kinsman (3:12-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Ruth asked of Boaz and how he answered?

topics.name: Boaz redeems and marries Ruth
topics.description: At the gate Boaz offers the nearer kinsman the right to redeem Elimelech's land and take Ruth; he declines, Boaz buys it and takes Ruth as his wife, and their son Obed is born, in the line leading to David.
evidence: Describe what happened at the gate
Say what the people and women said (4:11-15)
Trace the line from Pharez to David (4:18-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Boaz redeemed Ruth and how the book links her to David?

topics.name: 1 Samuel: overview
topics.description: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
evidence: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?

topics.name: Hannah prays for a son
topics.description: Childless Hannah prays at Shiloh and vows to give a son to the LORD; Eli blesses her, Samuel is born, and after he is weaned she brings him to serve the LORD at Shiloh.
evidence: Retell what Hannah asked and vowed (1:10-11)
Say what Hannah did when Samuel was weaned (1:24-28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Hannah prayed for a child and what she did when God gave Samuel?

topics.name: Hannah's song
topics.description: Hannah praises the LORD as holy and a rock, who kills and makes alive, brings low and lifts up, raises the poor and breaks his adversaries, and gives strength to his king.
evidence: Say what Hannah says about the LORD (2:2)
Name some reversals she describes (2:4-8)
Say what she says about the LORD's king and anointed (2:10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Hannah's song teaches about the LORD?

topics.name: Eli's wicked sons and the word against his house
topics.description: Hophni and Phinehas abuse the sacrifices and the women at the tabernacle while Samuel grows in favour; a man of God tells Eli that the LORD will cut off his house, and that both sons will die in one day.
evidence: Say what Eli's sons did wrong (2:12-17, 2:22)
Say what sign was given to Eli (2:34)
Say what the LORD promises about a faithful priest (2:35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why God judged Eli's house?

topics.name: The LORD calls Samuel
topics.description: The LORD calls the boy Samuel three times before Eli tells him how to answer; the LORD tells him he will judge Eli's house, Samuel tells Eli everything, and all Israel knows he is a prophet.
evidence: Retell how Samuel heard the LORD
Say what Samuel said when he finally answered (3:10)
Say what the LORD told Samuel and how Eli responded (3:11-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how God called Samuel in the night?

topics.name: The ark is captured and Eli dies
topics.description: Israel is defeated by the Philistines, brings the ark of the covenant from Shiloh to the camp, loses it as Hophni and Phinehas are killed, and Eli dies on hearing the news; Phinehas' wife names her son Ichabod.
evidence: Say why Israel fetched the ark and what happened (4:3-11)
Say what happened to Eli and his sons (4:11-18)
Say what Ichabod means in the text (4:21-22)

dependencies.reason: The overview sets out the book that chapter 1 begins
Joshua 1:6 speaks of the land the LORD swore to give to the fathers
Joshua 2:1 describes Joshua sending the spies after the charge to enter the land in chapter 1
Joshua 1:11 commands the people to prepare to pass over the Jordan within three days
Joshua 3:1 follows the spies' return to Joshua at Shittim in 2:23-24
Joshua 4:19 puts Israel at Gilgal after the crossing and chapter 5 continues there
Joshua 6:2 follows the meeting with the captain of the LORD's host in 5:13-15 near Jericho
Joshua 6:17 and 6:22-25 keep the oath given to Rahab in chapter 2
Achan took of the accursed thing from Jericho, which was forbidden in Joshua 6:18
Joshua 8:1 follows the defeat at Ai and the removal of Achan in chapter 7
Joshua 8:30 begins "Then" after the taking of Ai in 8:1-29
Joshua 9:3 says Gibeon acted after hearing what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai
Joshua 10:4-6 has the kings attack Gibeon because it made peace with Israel, and Gibeon calls on Joshua
Joshua 10:28 begins with Makkedah, where the five kings were hanged in 10:16-27
Joshua 11:1 follows the southern victories reported in chapter 10
Joshua 12 sums up the victories described in chapters 6-11
Joshua 13:1 follows the summary of conquest in chapters 11-12
Joshua 14:1-5 describes the land division by lot that begins after chapter 13
Caleb's portion in Judah is given in Joshua 14:13 and 15:13-14
Joshua 16:1 gives the lot of the children of Joseph after Judah's lot in chapter 15
Joshua 18:2 says seven tribes still had no inheritance after Judah and Joseph's lots
